+## Revsets
+
+Revsets (sets of revisions) are how jj addresses commits. A
+revision is identified by `@`, a chid, or a cid, and revsets are
+built from those identifiers plus the operators `-`, `+`, `..`,
+and `::`. There is a complete language available — see
+`jj help -k revsets`.
+
+Summary:
+
+- A revision (rev) is used for addressing/referring to commits.
+- jj supports a change_id (chid) and commit_id (cid).
+  - The chid is permanent and doesn't change.
+  - The cid is the SHA of the current commit and changes with any
+    change to it or its ancestors.
+- A revset is a set of revisions.
+- In many jj commands revsets can address multiple commits.
+- There is one root commit; chid=zzz sha=0 owner=root.
+- The root commit never has content nor description.
+- There can be multiple independent lineages of commits off root():
+  - to create:
+    - `jj new 'root()'`
+    - `git switch --orphan <name>`
+  - to see these:
+    - `jj log -r 'roots(~root())'`
+    - `git log --all --max-parents=0 --oneline`
+
+The examples below show these primitives in action.
+

+
+Some examples of revisions/rev:
+   - @, chid=tkpvsrop, cid=ad2ba9b4 is the current commit
+   - @-, chid=wxtmosqz, cid=35ac2422 is the ancestor of the current commit
+   - @--, chid=vktlnyvm, cid=a0b0285e is the ancestor of the ancestor and so on
+
+```
+$ jj log -r 'all()'
+@  tkpvsrop wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 ad2ba9b4
+│  count 3
+○  wxtmosqz wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 35ac2422
+│  count 2
+○  vktlnyvm wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 a0b0285e
+│  count 1
+○  nvwytkrw wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 base 54fd18f7
+│  count 0
+◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000
+```
+
+Move @ to vktlnyvm. (This could also have been done with `jj edit -r @--`.)
+
+```

+Working copy  (@) now at: vktlnyvm a0b0285e count 1
+Parent commit (@-)      : nvwytkrw 54fd18f7 base | count 0
+```
+

+
+```
+$ jj log -r @
+@  vktlnyvm count 1
+$ jj log -r @-
+○  nvwytkrw base | count 0
+$ jj log -r @--
+◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000
+$ jj log -r @+
+○  wxtmosqz count 2
+$ jj log -r @++
+○  tkpvsrop count 3
+$ jj log -r @+++      # empty — nothing that far out
+$ jj log -r @---      # empty
+$ jj log -r @..
+○  tkpvsrop count 3
+○  wxtmosqz count 2
+$ jj log -r @::
+○  tkpvsrop count 3
+○  wxtmosqz count 2
+@  vktlnyvm count 1
+$ jj log -r ..@
+@  vktlnyvm count 1
+○  nvwytkrw base | count 0
+$ jj log -r ::@
+@  vktlnyvm count 1
+○  nvwytkrw base | count 0
+◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000
+```

+
+- `@-` and `@--` resolve to single revisions: parent and
+  grandparent of @. `@+` and `@++` are children. The blank output
+  for `@+++` and `@---` is the empty revset — there is no revision
+  that far away in this chain.
+- `@..` and `@::` are ranges going outward from @ toward
+  descendants:
+  - `@..` is the *open* form: descendants of @, **excluding** @
+    itself (here: count 2 and count 3).
+  - `@::` is the *closed* form: descendants of @, **including** @
+    itself (here: @=count 1, count 2, count 3).

+○  nvwytkrw base | count 0

+○  tkpvsrop count 3
+○  wxtmosqz count 2

+@  vktlnyvm count 1
+○  nvwytkrw base | count 0

Commit both repos, push the work repo's BOOKMARK, and
squash-push the bot repo's `main` — one resumable command.

Collapses the manual commit-push-publish ceremony into a
single subcommand with two interactive approval gates and a
state machine with persistent progress so interruptions can
resume without re-doing completed stages.

Stages: preflight (tracking / bot-published / sync checks —
no build steps; run project checks yourself before pushing)
→ review (approve diff)
→ message ($EDITOR / --title+--body, approve text) →
commit-work → commit-bot (skipped if clean) → bookmark-set
(work repo → <bookmark>, bot repo → main) → push-work →
squash-push-bot. Failures in commit-work / commit-bot /
bookmark-set roll both repos back via
`jj op restore` to the snapshot recorded before commit-work.
After push-work succeeds the remote boundary is crossed and
recovery is forward-only.

Non-interactive use: pass both --title and --body plus --yes
to skip the review gate. Saved state carries title/body
across resumes so only the first invocation needs them.

Usage: vc-x1 push [OPTIONS] [BOOKMARK]

Arguments:
  [BOOKMARK]
          Bookmark to advance in the work repo (positional form of
          `--bookmark`). The bot repo always advances `main`.
          
          Accepting a positional lets the common case read as `vc-x1 push main`
          without the `--bookmark` ceremony; `--bookmark` is kept as an alias
          for scripts and for composition with other args. The two forms
          conflict if both supplied.

Options:
      --bookmark <BOOKMARK>
          Bookmark to advance in the work repo (flag form; see positional)

  -V, --version
          Print the `vc-x1 X.Y.Z` banner as the first line, then continue. With
          no subcommand, prints the banner and exits.
          
          Replaces clap's auto-version (which would exit after printing): the
          banner now rides along with normal subcommand execution rather than
          gating it, so scripts can capture the version *and* the command's
          output in one invocation.

      --restart
          Clear any saved state file and start from stage 1

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --from <STAGE>
          Explicit stage to jump to (advanced / debug use)

          Possible values:
          - preflight:       Verify bookmark tracking, the bot-published
            invariant, and sync state
          - review:          Present diff for the first approval gate
          - message:         Compose / edit the commit message; present for
            second gate
          - commit-work:     Commit the work repo
          - commit-bot:      Commit the `.claude` bot repo (skipped if empty)
          - bookmark-set:    Advance each repo's bookmark to its `@-`: work →
            `<bookmark>`, bot → `main`
          - push-work:       `jj git push --bookmark <b> -R .`
          - squash-push-bot: In-process squash of `.claude`'s trailing session
            writes + push `main`

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

      --step
          Pause between every stage for an interactive approval gate

      --status
          Print where the saved state thinks we are and exit

      --recheck
          Re-run `preflight` even on resume (default: skip if last run
          succeeded)

      --no-squash-push
          Stop before `squash-push-bot` so it can be run manually

      --dry-run
          Print the exact commands for every stage without side effects

      --title <STR>
          Commit title (skip `$EDITOR` for the message stage)

      --body <STR>
          Commit body (skip `$EDITOR` for the message stage)

  -y, --yes
          Auto-approve interactive prompts (review gate, message-edit
          confirmation). Required when `--title` / `--body` aren't both supplied
          in non-interactive contexts

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Everything checkable in the proposal verifies, and the command shape is right. I have one substantive reservation about the body, and one protocol item the push is currently missing. No edits made — thoughts only, as asked.

**What verifies:**

- The sha256 manifest is accurate. All three repos' shared docs are byte-identical right now, and the 12-hex prefixes in the body match what I computed: AGENTS.md `5381e6c44181`, cycle-protocol.md `f76b5b39cbd1`, jj-tips.md `813d403db5ed`. (This also confirms iiac-perf adopted the smoothed run-on fix — their jj-tips.md hashes identical to ours.) Using file content hashes rather than commit SHAs is a nice touch: they're stable across commits, sidestep the can't-self-reference problem, and let any repo verify convergence later.
- The command itself is sound. Title is 38 cols, body wraps ≤72, no hand-written ochid (push injects it). `--title`/`--body` only skip `$EDITOR`; without `--yes` the diff-review and message gates stay interactive, which matches the pushing policy. The `$(cat …)` substitution is safe — quotes and backticks inside the files are data, not shell syntax.

**My reservation — the body vs the file-by-file convention.** Our convention says a work-repo commit body is the mechanical record of *that commit*: one bullet per file changed. This template's commit touches exactly two files (one AGENTS.md line, three jj-tips.md fixes) — but the proposed body carries a full `notes/cycle-protocol.md` bullet group (this commit doesn't touch that file; it converged in `a680ff8`) and AGENTS.md bullets (terminology, preflight, unwrap) that also landed here in `a680ff8`. `git show` of this commit will disagree with its own body, and the hedge sentence ("the template took only the fixes") acknowledges that without curing it. I'd keep the **title identical across all three repos** (that's the greppable convergence marker), keep the intro and the sha manifest shared, but make the file bullets **per-repo** — here just the two files, with one intro sentence noting the doc-set rewrite itself landed in `a680ff8`. Identical bodies everywhere have appeal, but since each repo's diff differs anyway, the shared body is already per-repo inaccurate; title + sha manifest carry the convergence identity fine.

**Protocol gap regardless of body choice — the Commits backfill.** `chores-01.md` has `## docs: shared protocol set; template cleanup` with an empty `Commits:`, and `a680ff86683d` is now permanent on `main@origin`. Per the backfill convention, this push should include the chores-01.md edit adding `Commits: [[N]]` plus the `[N]: <commit-url>/a680ff86683d "<full-40-hex>"` definition. For consistency with that precedent, this commit arguably also wants its own short chores section (`## docs: converge shared protocol doc set`, empty `Commits:`) to be backfilled next push.

**Minor note:** the help shows one message stage feeding both `commit-work` and `commit-bot`, so the bot-repo commit will presumably carry this same work-repo-shaped body rather than "in-session activity" bullets. I assume that's known vc-x1 behavior, just flagging it.

Bottom line: I'd trim the body's bullets to this repo's diff, add the chores-01.md backfill (and optionally the new section) to the working copy before pushing, and then the suggested command is exactly right.

Chores-XX files use [Prose form](../../AGENTS.md#prose-form). They
contain discussions and notes on various chores in github compatible
markdown. There is also a [todo.md](../todo.md) file that tracks

with the why and how this task will be completed.

## docs: shared protocol set; template cleanup

Commits:

vc-x1: the shared protocol set — `AGENTS.md`,

  written as two words, hyphenated only when the pair sits
  directly in front of another noun. Defined once in AGENTS.md
  Project Structure; all variants (app repo, session repo,
  code-side, `.claude` repo) swept from the living docs.

  `squash-push` replaces the detached `finalize` flow, push
  preflight is repo-state-only (the medium's validation is the

  directive rather than every push.
